title: Which numbers do the idli and vada players say?
description: In a counting game, every third number is replaced by idli and every fifth by vada. Skip counting along a number strip shows which numbers get each word, and Keeko's doubt, that idli goes only with the numbers that go into three, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: idli and vada numbers come from skip counting, and such numbers are called multiples. Watch for students who list the numbers that go into three instead of counting on past three.

source: In the idli-vada game, for which numbers do the players say
video_script.why: The child sees that the idli numbers and the vada numbers come from skip counting in threes and in fives, and that such numbers are called multiples.
video_script.substitution: A multiple of a number is a number you reach by skip counting in steps of that number.
video_script.anchor: the idli-vada game of the book: children sit in a circle and count aloud
video_script.wrong_answer: idli is said for one and three, the numbers that go into three
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says idli is said only for one and three, the numbers that go into three. The game keeps going past three, so skip counting must carry on to six, nine and more, and the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Idli is said for the multiples of three, and vada for the multiples of five

final_answer.value: idli: multiples of 3; vada: multiples of 5
final_answer.spoken: idli is said for the multiples of three, and vada for the multiples of five

never_show: the label multiples of 3 or multiples of 5 before the answer
maths_rules: idli is said at every 3rd number: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21 and so on, the multiples of 3
vada is said at every 5th number: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and so on, the multiples of 5
ground demo: skip counting in 2s gives 2, 4, 6, 8, the multiples of 2
slip: 1 and 3 are the numbers that go into 3; the idli numbers come from counting on in steps of 3
video_script.design: One idea: skip counting in steps of a number gives its multiples. Assumes the child can skip count. Wrong idea: the idli numbers are the numbers that go into three. The number strip stays to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; children sit in a circle and a number strip is hidden in the anchor band

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.circle: children appear sitting in a circle
marks.third: the words every third number becomes idli appear
marks.fifth: the words every fifth number becomes vada appear
marks.ask: the words which numbers get idli and which get vada appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the idli-vada game.
<bookmark mark='circle'/>Children sit in a circle and count numbers aloud, one after another.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Every third number is replaced by the word idli.
<bookmark mark='fifth'/>Every fifth number is replaced by the word vada.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>For which numbers do the players say idli, and for which do they say vada?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a number strip from 0 to 10; jumps of 2 land on 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and each landing glows; the label multiples of 2 appears

marks.twos: jumps of 2 along the strip land on 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 and each landing glows
marks.name: the label multiples of 2 appears above the glowing numbers
marks.all: the words skip counting appear beside the jumps

narration: <bookmark mark='twos'/>Think of counting in twos along a number strip: two, four, six, eight.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A number you reach by skip counting like this is called a multiple.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Here, two, four, six and eight are multiples of two.

beats.on_screen: Given: idli for every 3rd number, vada for every 5th number

marks.given: the two rules are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the players say idli for every third number and vada for every fifth number.

beats.on_screen: To find: the numbers that get idli and the numbers that get vada

marks.find: the words To find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the numbers that get idli and the numbers that get vada.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: skip count in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, ... each landing is circled in teal and labelled idli

marks.threes: jumps of 3 start along the number strip
marks.list: the landings 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21 are circled and labelled idli

narration: <bookmark mark='threes'/>Step one, skip count in threes, because idli is said at every third number.
<bookmark mark='list'/>We land on three, six, nine, twelve, fifteen, eighteen and twenty one. The count goes on.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: skip count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, ... each landing is circled in orange and labelled vada

marks.fives: jumps of 5 start along the number strip
marks.list: the landings 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 are circled and labelled vada

narration: <bookmark mark='fives'/>Step two, skip count in fives, because vada is said at every fifth number.
<bookmark mark='list'/>We land on five, ten, fifteen, twenty and twenty five. This count goes on too.

beats.on_screen: Answer: idli for the multiples of 3, vada for the multiples of 5

marks.ans: the answer is boxed and the two labels read multiples of 3 and multiples of 5

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Idli is said for the multiples of three, and vada for the multiples of five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble, then struck through; the strip carries on past 3 to 15 and idli is still said beyond 3

marks.doubt: the bubble appears with idli at 1 and 3
marks.fix: the strip carries on past 3 and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks idli is said for one and three, the numbers that go into three.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the game does not stop at three, because the children keep counting.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Idli must come again at six, nine and more. We must keep counting on in threes.
